messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: route-fallback-errors-prod (severity: P2). Symptoms: embeddings requests being routed to chat/instruct variant; ~45% 5xx on /v1/embeddings since 11:42 UTC. Auto-escalation to #incidents at 11:43

pagerduty: paging rohan. oncall: rohan (SRE) primary, mira (infra) secondary.

rohan: I'm on it. grabbing context and linking traces. can someone paste the most recent routing policy change?

mira: showing recent commit to routing-catalog (deploy 11:38 UTC):
```
- alias: embeddings-frontend
  preferred: embed-v2
  fallbacks: [embed-v1, chat-instruct-v1]  # <-- fallback order changed accidentally
  pinned_version: embed-v2-2026-03-11
```
looks like fallback order was tightened, and chat-instruct ended up in the fallback list.

kai: confirmed. infra logs show a model-variant mapping change at 11:37:58 that added `chat-instruct-v1` to fallback set for embeddings alias. change author: `release-automation` (auto merge).

jess: impact numbers: traffic to /v1/embeddings: 3.4k rps. Error rate jumped from 0.2% -> 42% between 11:42-11:50. Affected regions: eu-west-1 and us-east-1 (primary). Customers reporting search & similarity failures.

luis: CC product: one enterprise tenant (tenant-id: t-93d1) saw 15% request loss and alerted support.

rohan: immediate mitigation options: 1) remove `chat-instruct-v1` from embedding fallbacks in routing-catalog and roll out. 2) pin alias->embed-v1 override for affected routes. 3) disable fallback policy globally (risky). I will take lead on option 1 and 2 in parallel.

mira: to be safe, I recommend forcing an override on the edge LB routes for /v1/embeddings to `embed-v1` while we patch the catalog. less time than a full catalog deploy.

kai: adding commands: run `confctl set route /v1/embeddings model=embed-v1 --scope=prod --ttl=1800` (this forces override for 30m). I'll prep the confctl session.

rohan: executing now.
```
rohan: sh> confctl set route /v1/embeddings model=embed-v1 --scope=prod --ttl=1800
OK: override applied (txn 4589)
```

mira: overrides accepted by edge: routing logs show embed-v1 being selected now. error rate dropping already.

jess: metric update: error rate down from 42% -> 3.8% over 2m after override. p95 latency for embeddings stable.

luis: notifying impacted customer channel and support-runbook: "We're mitigating — forcing correct embedding model while we fix fallback policy."

oncall-manager: good. rohan, escalate to infra oncall for catalog patch. mira, coordinate rollback of risky automation.

mira: investigating automation: release-automation job included a stale fallback list from template `fallbacks.yml`. I'll revoke its ability to edit routing-catalog until we patch template.

kai: digging into why chat-instruct landed in fallbacks: alias normalization bug in templating substituted `{{default_fallbacks}}` with a combined list that incorrectly included `chat-instruct-v1` for interface type 'embed'. patch ready: remove interface-agnostic fallbacks and add validation that fallbacks are compatible with interface (embed vs gen/chat).

rohan: plan of record:
- short term: edge override (done) -> restores customer traffic.
- medium term: patch templating + validation -> block incompatible fallback entries (PR ready).
- long term: add unit/e2e test to routing deploys that rejects interface-mismatched fallbacks.

jess: running warm restart of routing-catalog deploy with the fix now (dry-run first).

mira: dry-run passed. scheduling canary rollout to prod: 1 host in us-east-1 at 12:05 UTC.

kai: also added alert rule: `routing.fallback.incompatible_count > 0` to fire to #incidents. will create a runbook link.

luis: support message posted to customers: "We've applied a temporary routing override to restore embeddings. We're rolling a fix to prevent incompatible model fallbacks. ETA for full remediation: ~40-60 minutes."

rohan: tracking customer impact: total requests impacted ~120k, error responses ~52k during window. major customers affected: t-93d1 (15% loss), t-22a7 (search latency increase). Not seeing data exfil or PII exposure.

jess: can we remove the confctl override after catalog roll out and validation? want to avoid drift.

mira: yes. after canary validation (10m), we'll remove override. procedure:
1) deploy patch to routing-catalog (canary)
2) wait 10m, check `errors` and `route_selection` logs
3) remove confctl override if traffic stable
4) full rollout

rohan: canary looks good at 12:12 UTC. embedding error rate maintained ~0.3%. I'm going to remove the override.

rohan: sh> confctl delete override /v1/embeddings --scope=prod --txn=4592
OK: override removed

jess: after override removal, error rate still low. routing logs show embed-v1 selected by catalog on all requests.

mira: patched `fallbacks.yml` template and disabled `release-automation` write perms. PR (#4521) merged at 12:24 UTC.

kai: adding post-incident action items: 1) add validation for interface compatibility in routing CI. 2) audit fallback lists across aliases. 3) restrict automation roles. 4) add a canary guard for catalog entries that include cross-interface fallbacks.

luis: support closing the critical customer tickets. sent post-mortem summary to affected customers and onboarded them to status page.

oncall-manager: excellent remediation. rohan, paste final timeline and assign P0->P1 tasks to owners.

rohan: TL;DR timeline:
- 11:37:58 UTC - release-automation merged template with bad fallback list
- 11:42 UTC - errors spike for embeddings (5xx)
- 11:43 UTC - pager -> #incidents channel
- 11:50 UTC - edge override applied to force embed-v1
- 12:05 UTC - canary of catalog patch
- 12:12 UTC - override removed after successful canary
- 12:24 UTC - patch merged + automation perms restricted

rohan: Owners -> pia (product) for customer comms (luis already handling), mira for automation perms, kai for CI validation, jess for metrics dashboarding. I'll file the postmortem template.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged and logged: INC-2026-03-11-0472. Postmortem required within 72h.

rohan: closing incident thread. monitoring for 24h. thanks all. :thumbsup:
